title: Buddy Bolden at Johnson Park
summary: He remembers Bolden's rough band at Johnson Park beside Robichaux at Lincoln Park, and the mud on Carrollton Avenue.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Do you remember hearing a band that Buddy Bolden...
Yes, sir. He used to play at Lincoln Park. Buddy Bolden played at Lincoln... at Johnson Park and Robichaux played at Lincoln Park. It was right joining. Yeah.
What kind of a band that Bolden...
Rough one, that's...
Really rough.

Really rough. Yeah. Robichaux had nice orchestras, you know, nice dance music. And Bolden, the sticky cornered out the window, you know, and Hoopner, everybody go over there. That's the way they used it. That was at Lincoln Park. It's one block north of the inbound track on Carlton Avenue.
Yeah, I know where that is. I went out and looked. There's nothing there now.
That Hill Store used to be there.
Sort of a big... Some public building is there. It is now. They changed that? Something there, yeah. For Lincoln Park.
At Oleand and Carlton.
That's the corner. And they showed me where Johnson Park... People live there now.
Yes.
Home is where Johnson Park is.
We used to go back to Lincoln Park, mud up to our knees on Carlton Avenue.
You did what? How was that?
Mud up to your knees when it ran.
Mud up to your knees.
It sank that much in mud on Carlton Avenue.
Do you remember who else was in Bolden's band?
No, sir. I didn't know any of it.
You know how big a band it was? How many people?
Seven.
